Job Description: Project Manager – Global Security Strategic Initiatives

Duration: 06 Months

Location: North Chicago, IL 60064 (Hybrid)

Overview
:
The Project Manager will play a key role in leading and coordinating enterprise level initiatives including Global Security transformation efforts, strategic technology projects, and other cross-functional initiatives approved through the Project Management Office (PMO) governance.
This role requires a PM who can manage complexity, enable executive decision-making, and drive disciplined execution across multiple high?visibility initiatives—often operating with incomplete information, evolving scope, and senior stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:

• Serve as project manager for multiple concurrent initiatives across the Global Security strategic portfolio, including transformation, technology enablement, and operational improvement efforts
• Translate leadership direction into clear project plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and execution timelines.
• Maintain project visibility and accountability, drafting and updating core project documentation (e.g., 4?ups, business cases, project plans, RAIDs etc), facilitating stakeholder meetings, and following up with owners to ensure progress and closure.
• Manage and track progress across multiple initiatives, overseeing project intake, scheduling, timelines, milestones, and meeting cadence in alignment with Global Security PMO processes, while proactively surfacing risks, tradeoffs, and capacity considerations to support timely decision?making.
• Arrange and facilitate regular stakeholder meetings.
• Measure project outcomes and success against organizational goals.
• Prepare materials for Steering Committee and leadership meetings, including status updates, decision briefs, risk summaries, and options analysis.
• Partner with cross?functional stakeholders including Business Technology Services (BTS), HR, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, EHS, Facilities, and regional Security teams to coordinate execution.
• Ensure technical, policy, training, and compliance requirements are identified and incorporated into project plans, partnering with stakeholders to support change communications, enable user adoption, and minimize resistance.
• Ensure project governance, process documentation, and training resources are developed, stored, and shared as appropriate.

Qualifications and Essential Skills, Experience, and Competencies

• Degree in a relevant subject area or equivalent experience gained through enterprise project or transformation work.
• 6+ years of experience managing complex, cross?functional projects or programs, with a demonstrated ability to move work forward in environments where priorities evolve.
• Proven ability to manage multiple initiatives at the same time, balancing scope, timelines, and capacity while keeping leadership informed of risks and tradeoffs.
• Strong business and operational acumen, with the ability to anticipate organizational needs, connect work to strategic intent, and help leaders make informed decisions.
• Experience leading or supporting enterprise?level initiatives in transformation, technology enablement, regulated environments, or security?adjacent functions.
• Comfortable working with senior leaders, governance bodies, and steering committees, including preparing leadership?ready materials and supporting decision?making forums.
• Strong cross?functional collaboration skills, with experience partnering across teams such as Technology, HR, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, EHS, Facilities, and regional operations to coordinate execution.
• Experience supporting or leading change management and communications efforts, including policy rollouts, training coordination, and adoption planning.
• Familiarity with security, compliance?driven, or regulated environments is strongly preferred, including comfort navigating risk, controls, audits, and policy requirements (deep technical expertise is not required).
• Strong understanding of project governance, portfolio management, and change management principles, with a bias toward disciplined execution and transparency.
• Clear, concise communicator with strong organizational skills and attention to detail, able to distill complexity into actionable next steps.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel); experience with Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, or similar tools is a plus.
• Familiarity with security or enterprise systems (e.g., access management platforms, incident or mass?notification systems) is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

• Leadership has clear visibility into priorities, risks, and capacity, and can make informed decisions without surprise.
• Strategic initiatives move from approval to delivery with disciplined governance and minimal rework.
• Pilots result in clear scale / stop decisions and repeatable rollout plans.
• Cross?functional stakeholders view the PMO as a decision?enablement partner, not a reporting function.

What are the top 3-5 skills, experience or education required for this position:

1. Enterprise Project & Portfolio Management (Non Negotiable)

• Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with competing priorities using a structured intake, sequencing, and delivery model.
• Comfortable operating at both project level execution and portfolio level tradeoff discussions (capacity, priority, timing).
• Experience supporting PMO governance, not just running isolated projects.
2. Executive & Steering Committee Enablement

• Demonstrated experience preparing leadership ready materials: decision briefs, status summaries, risks/tradeoffs, and options—not raw project updates.
• Skilled at framing work so leaders can clearly answer: approve, defer, change scope, or stop.
• Comfortable facilitating governance forums (SteerCo, leadership reviews) and following through on decisions.
3. Cross Functional Influence & Change Management

• Strong ability to work across Security, BTS, HR, Legal, Compliance, EHS, Facilities, and Regions—without formal authority.
• Experience supporting change management, communications, and training rollouts, especially where policy or behavior change is involved.
• Understands that adoption risk is just as critical as technical delivery.
4. Comfort in Regulated / Security Adjacent Environments

• Familiarity with security, compliance driven, or regulated environments (physical security, IT/security systems, pharma, manufacturing, privacy, safety).
• Understands concepts like risk, controls, audits, access management, and policy enforcement—even if they are not the technical expert.
5. Structured Thinking + Comfort with Ambiguity

? Ability to bring structure to unclear work, especially early stage initiatives coming out of Phoenix, AI exploration, or strategy discussions.
? Strong judgment on when to add rigor vs. keep things light, depending on risk and scale.
? Proactive, self directed, and comfortable iterating as strategy evolves.

Bonne compréhension des principes de gestion du changement organisationnel.
Maîtrise d’outils de gestion de projet et portefeuille tels que MS Project / EPM.
Excellentes compétences en documentation et présentation.

Baccalauréat en administration, finance, opérations, gestion ou domaine connexe.

Certification en gestion de projet, telle que PMP ou équivalent.
Expérience avec des initiatives de Marketing Operations.
Connaissance des plateformes CMS, DAM et personnalisation.

Expérience avec les données de prospects et fournisseurs de données externes.
Compréhension des enjeux de qualité des données, consentement et confidentialité.
Connaissance de la gouvernance de l’IA.

Expérience avec les opérations et workflows de contenu.

Piloter les initiatives de la planification jusqu’à leur mise en production et clôture.

jobs.title: Founding Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
About Kaizen

Kaizen is a digital employee that helps healthcare providers get patients into care faster. It processes referrals, verifies insurance benefits, manages prior authorizations, and handles provider credentialing across the systems teams already use. Customers can give Kaizen feedback directly, teaching it their processes and refining how it works.

We recently raised $8.5M from Joe Lonsdale’s 8VC, Y Combinator, Jeff Dean, and Eric Schmidt’s Innovation Endeavors.
We’re hiring our first Deployment Strategist to help $100M+ healthcare providers drive seven-figure ROI with AI.

The opportunity

You’ll work directly with healthcare executives to identify where automation can create the most value, then use Kaizen to deliver it. With a digital employee that learns from customer feedback, you can deploy workflows in just two weeks that generate six figures in annual value
.

Your job is to understand the customer’s business, identify the right opportunities, and teach Kaizen how to execute. You’ll be equally comfortable discussing an ROI model with a CFO and sitting alongside an authorization specialist to understand why a case is stuck.

As Kaizen’s first Deployment Strategist
, you’ll work directly with the founders to build the function: how we deploy, how we measure success, and how we turn successful deployments into broader customer relationships. As we grow, you’ll have the opportunity to recruit, mentor, and lead the team around you.

What you’ll do

Find the highest-value opportunities.
Map customer operations, identify bottlenecks that delay care or leave revenue uncollected, and build a deployment roadmap tied to measurable business outcomes.
Teach Kaizen how the customer works.
Turn customer processes into live workflows, from processing referral faxes and checking benefits to submitting authorizations and completing provider enrollment applications. Help customers give feedback directly so Kaizen keeps improving.
Get deep into the details.
Learn the payer-specific requirements, system quirks, and exceptions that determine whether a workflow succeeds. Trace failures, close gaps, and make sure the automation works in the conditions customers actually face.
Own customer results.
Establish a baseline, agree on success metrics, and track improvements in processing time, staff capacity, and revenue. Use the results to guide expansion.
Lead the relationship.
Earn trust with executives and frontline teams, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and keep deployments moving when priorities or requirements change.
Build the function.
Establish our deployment practices, turn successful approaches into repeatable playbooks, and help hire and mentor future Deployment Strategists.
Influence the product.
Work closely with the founders and Engineering to solve recurring problems and translate customer needs into product improvements.

What you’ll bring

2+ years bringing software into the real world.
You’ve worked in solutions engineering, technical product management, integrations, software consulting, or AI deployment. You’ve translated business needs into working systems and stayed involved through launch.
Business judgment and executive communication.
You can work with healthcare leaders to identify opportunities to grow revenue, from converting more referrals into visits to preventing authorization delays and getting providers enrolled with payers sooner. You can quantify the opportunity and make a clear, compelling case to decision-makers.
Hands-on AI experience.
You’ve built or deployed solutions using LLMs, generative AI, or machine learning. You can explain how they work, evaluate their performance, and troubleshoot failures to make them reliable in practice.
Ownership and follow-through.
You take responsibility for outcomes, hold a high standard, and help others do their best work. You’re comfortable figuring out what needs to happen and driving it forward.

Experience deploying AI within a consulting firm or working with healthcare organizations is especially relevant. Healthcare experience isn’t required; curiosity about how care gets delivered is.

Why Kaizen

Build a function from the ground up, work directly with the founders, and own consequential customer relationships early in your career. You’ll have a product that lets you move quickly and a direct connection between your work and its impact: patients getting care sooner, staff spending less time on paperwork, and providers getting paid for the care they deliver.

jobs.title: Nordic Corporate Security Manager
jobs.description:
Shape the future of security across the Nordics in a fast-growing, international business.

Verisure is seeking a highly experienced, strategic and hands-on Nordic Corporate Security Manager to lead and develop our physical security agenda across the Nordic region. This is a critical role with high visibility, supporting senior leadership and enabling continued growth in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

This is a rare opportunity to step into a high-growth, high-performing and profitable business with a clear mission: to protect what matters most.
Verisure operates in a category with remarkably low market penetration, offering fast potential for expansion. Our growth is rapid, resilient, and highly profitable — powered by a recurring revenue model and deep, long-term customer relationships. What sets Verisure apart is the strength of our platform: a robust, scalable operating model and a high-performing culture rooted in purpose. We’re growing fast, we’re doing it right — and we’re still just getting started.

About Verisure

Verisure is the leading provider of professionally monitored security services with 24/7 response in Europe and Latin America.
Every day, our dedicated teams use leading technology to Deter, Detect, Verify and Intervene to protect our residential and small business customers against intrusion, burglary, fires, physical attack, home occupation, theft from a business, life-threatening emergencies and other hazards that may risk the safety, wellbeing or condition of our customers and their properties.

We protect a portfolio of over 6.3 million customers across 18 countries.
In 14 of our 18 geographies, we lead the category in terms of customers served and we continue to gain market share. We have a strong track record of profitable and resilient growth, primarily delivered organically by our codified and industrialised business model with high share of recurring revenues (about 90%) and industry leading retention.

Our mission is to give our customers peace of mind by protecting what matters most to them. We believe that everyone has the right to feel safe and secure.

For the year ended 31 December 2025, Verisure delivered another year of strong, profitable growth, generating €3.7 billion in Total Revenue, €1.7 billion in Adjusted EBITDA (46% margin) and €953 million in Adjusted EBIT (25% margin). For more information:  www.verisure.com

Verisure in the Nordics

Born in Sweden over 35 years ago, Verisure has grown from a local pioneer into the leading provider of monitored security solutions across the Nordic region and globally.
Today, Sweden stands as our third largest market and Norway as our fifth, with Denmark and Finland playing critical strategic roles in our portfolio. All four countries have delivered exceptional growth over the past five years and hold #1 positions in their respective markets.

With more than 2,000 passionate colleagues and partners across the Nordics, we proudly protect homes and small businesses every day.
As we continue to scale and accelerate, strengthening our brand, reputation, and trust with customers, communities, and key stakeholders is essential. Our ambition is clear: to make the Nordics the most recognized and most preferred security provider in the region.

Responsibilities Of The Corporate Security Manager

As Nordic Security Manager, you hold full accountability for the Corporate Security function across the Nordic region, with a clear mandate to lead, shape, and continuously strengthen the overall security framework
. You are expected to define and drive the regional security strategy, ensuring it is not only aligned with global standards but also effectively translated into concrete actions, measurable outcomes, and consistent execution across all Nordic markets.

In this role, you are not only responsible for setting direction—you are expected to ensure delivery, follow-through, and tangible impact
. You will proactively identify risks, challenge existing ways of working, and implement robust frameworks that enhance resilience, protect critical assets, and support the business in achieving its strategic objectives.

You will operate in a highly cross-functional environment, working closely with senior stakeholders across Legal, HR, Technology, Information Security, and Compliance. As a trusted partner, you are expected to influence decision-making at a senior level, provide clear and actionable insights, and ensure that security is embedded into business processes rather than treated as a standalone function
. In parallel, you will collaborate with international peers and Group functions to drive consistency, share best practices, and contribute to the continuous evolution of the global security agenda.

Success in this role requires the ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on involvement
, taking ownership in critical situations while maintaining a long-term, proactive perspective on risk and security development.

Core responsibilities

jobs.title: Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Location:

4910 Tiedeman Road, Brooklyn Ohio

Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst

Position Summary

Our Cyber Threat Management team is part of Key's broader Cyber Defense function within Corporate Information Security. Cyber Defense's mission is simple: We aim to Deter, Detect, Deny, and Disrupt adversaries through proactive threat-centric defense.

This senior strategic role advances KeyBank's Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) program by converting external and internal threat information into forward looking intelligence that informs business decisions, cybersecurity strategy, control investments, and enterprise risk management. The analyst will maintain and refine intelligence requirements, assess the financial services threat landscape, and evaluate geopolitical developments and emerging technology risks that may affect KeyBank, its customers, its third-party ecosystem, and its long-term objectives.

The analyst will produce strategic forecasts, control gap assessments, executive level intelligence products, and decision support for senior leaders. The role will also support briefings for the Board and regulators, translate complex threats into clear business impact, and help leaders prioritize resources based on intelligence, exposure, and risk. Success requires strong judgment, research, writing, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to deliver accurate, concise, and complete assessments.

Key Responsibilities

Aggregate, evaluate, and synthesize threat intelligence from diverse sources such as open-source intelligence (OSINT), dark web forums, commercial feeds, and internal sources to identify relevant and actionable strategic insights for the organization.
Strategic Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Report Writing & Briefing - Produce forward looking assessments, executive summaries and strategic forecasts on adversaries, campaigns, geopolitical developments, regulatory concerns, and technology driven risks.
Establish feedback measures that assess whether intelligence products are timely, relevant, actionable, and aligned to stakeholder needs.
Analyze the financial services industry threat landscape, including threats to banking operations, customers, payments, third parties, critical infrastructure, and sector confidence.
Evaluate emerging technology risks involving technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud services, quantum computing).
Deep understanding of Threat Actor (TA) Tactics, Techniques, & Procedures (TTPs) and Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) utilized by cyber adversaries with the ability to identify new and novel TTP’s.
Provide intelligence support during significant incidents or emerging threat events by clarifying context, likely implications, and potential future developments.
Conduct threat to control gap assessments by comparing relevant adversary capabilities and attack paths with existing security controls, risk treatments, and business dependencies.
Familiarity with leveraging frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, D3FEND, Diamond Model, Kill Chain), security platforms like Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR), Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP), and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR).
Apply intelligence led prioritization to help focus defensive resources, control improvements, threat hunting, vulnerability management, exercises (tabletop, red / blue / purple), and risk decisions on the threats most relevant to KeyBank.
Partner with Cyber Defense, Security Engineering, Fraud, Third-Party Risk Management, Third-Party Security, Technology, Legal, and other teams to assess and communicate cyber risks.
Provide mentorship and technical guidance to junior analysts and cross functional partners.
Lead by example in fostering a culture of curiosity, rigor, and continuous learning within the CTI function.
Represent KeyBank within intelligence sharing communities, industry working groups, government partnerships, and peer collaboration forums.
Leverage external partnerships and intelligence exchanges to strengthen organizational awareness and preparedness.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field—or equivalent experience
5+ years in CTI.
Demonstrated experience managing intelligence requirements and producing strategic intelligence for senior decision makers.
Strong understanding of the financial services threat environment and the business, operational, customer, third-party, and regulatory impacts of cyber threats.
Experience assessing geopolitical risk, state-sponsored activity, and emerging technology risks in a business or security context.
Ability to connect threat information to security controls, business exposure, and risk-based priorities.
Strong analytical, research, and writing skills.
Ability to work independently and escalate risks appropriately.
Ability to communicate concisely, effectively and directly with executive management.

Preferred Certifications

GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI)
Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+)
CompTIA Security+

Compensation And Benefits

This position is eligible to earn a base salary in the range of $96,000.00 - $181,000.00 annually. Placement within the pay range may differ based upon various factors, including but not limited to skills, experience and geographic location. Compensation for this role also includes eligibility for incentive compensation which may include production, commission, and/or discretionary incentives.

Please click here for a list of benefits for which this position is eligible.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Data Analyst to join our Business Data Operations Division.

Business Data Operations Division (BDOD) is a large and diverse area of around 400 staff, collecting economic statistics from several million businesses a year. It is the foundation for most of the ONS’ core economic outputs, such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The primary role for the division is the data collection, editing and validation of survey data.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social, and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.

Job Description

A Data Analyst collects, organises and studies data to provide business insight.

Responsibilities Include

Build analytical pipelines for automated processing of data used for regular reporting.
Lead the production of regular data and insight products.
Lead on the development and delivery of robust quality control processes over our outputs including the use of automated tests to validate processing.
Design and build creative data visualisations to deliver actionable insights for our business users.
Lead on the development of Power BI data models
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to collect information to support the measurement of ONS performance e.g. KPIs, monthly, quarterly, and annual reports etc used to track ONS performance.
Lead the delivery of management information products, liaising with stakeholders and collecting user requirements.
Lead the development of system and user process documentation; developing new documentation as required and updates to existing documentation.
Line manage, develop and coach 1-2 Data Analysts within your team.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

Applying statistical and analytical tools and techniques
(Practitioner)

lead the development of valuable statistical and analytical insights and reports
identify and apply a range of statistical and analytical techniques and tools, and support others in applying them
quality assure statistical techniques and analytical outputs across a team
engage with stakeholders and share statistical and analytical techniques to increase understanding and trust

Developing code for analysis
(Practitioner)

design and implement the analytical approach, including code, using appropriate standards and tests
lead collaboration to review and improve analytical approaches, including shared code
guide others in producing analytical approach documentation, identifying improvements

Communicating between the technical and non-technical
(Practitioner)

listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations
manage active and reactive communication
support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

Data visualisation
(Practitioner)

use a range of data visualisations to simplify a complex story.
adapt a story to the needs of multidisciplinary stakeholders.
advise and support others in developing inclusive, accessible data visualisations that recognise different user needs.
suggest improvements to data visualisation processes and standards to increase efficiency and quality.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Communicating and Influencing
Making Effective Decisions
Working Together
Leadership

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

Python for Data Analysis

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £41,985, Office for National Statistics contributes £12,163 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our valued colleagues across the organisation.

Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that our careers site will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture.

Inclusion & Accessibility

At ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.

If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Experience and Technical skills.

Security Clearance

For ONS the requirement for SC clearance is to have been present in the UK for 3 consecutive years immediately prior to applying
and the department will consider eligibility by exception on a case-by-case basis. You will be asked to provide information regarding your UK residency during your application, and failure to provide this will result in your application being rejected.

At the point of SC application, you will need to provide or give access to the following evidence:

Departmental or company records (personnel files, staff reports, sick leave reports and security records)
UK criminal records covering both spent and unspent criminal records
Your credit and financial history with a credit reference agency
Security Services records

Please note: We will reach out to you once the advert has closed to confirm eligibility for this role, this will be via an e-mail. Please check you e-mails.

Visa Sponsorship

ONS are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants are expected to hold a valid right to work in the UK when employment commences. If you are applying on a time-limited visa, this will need to be valid for at least 18 months at point of application.

To work at the ONS, candidates must meet both UK right to work and security clearance requirements (where applicable).

If you are unsure whether you meet the appropriate right to work or security clearance eligibility criteria, please refer to the guidance on Gov.uk or contact the recruitment email provided in the advert before applying
. Failure to meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected and employment offers being withdrawn.

Application Process

Number of Stages: 2

Stage 1: Application

Stage 2: Interview

Stage 1 – Application

The assessment process at the application stage will be based on your work history, CV, skills, experience, and personal statement. It is important that your application is tailored to highlight the skills, knowledge, and experience relevant to the role.

A personal statement is required at application stage, the maximum word count allowed is 1,250 words, which should not be exceeded. You should provide evidence for each essential skill criterion listed in the person specification. As these criteria are scored, it is advisable to give clear examples for each one, including the impact of your actions, ideally utilising the STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

In instances where a high number of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted, and candidates will be invited to interview based on merit order, i.e., those with the highest scores.

Please note that Success Profiles Behaviour examples are not required at this stage of the application process.

When a high volume of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted. Candidates will be invited to interview based on their merit order, with those achieving the highest scores being prioritised. Applicants who score below the adjusted pass mark but still pass will be placed on hold and may be invited to interview at a later date.

We often have similar roles available at different grades. If a candidate is suitable for a similar role or a lower grade than they have applied for, we may offer the candidate that role without the need to go through a further selection process providing the role has the same behaviours, and essential skills.

Stage 2
– Interview

If invited to interview, you will be assessed using techniques aligned with the Civil Service Success Profiles framework, covering all behaviours listed in the job advert and any required technical skills.

You will be required to provide a 5 minute presentation at interview. The presentation topic will be emailed to candidates who have passed the initial online application stage, 1 week prior to interview. This presentation will assess candidates against the Technical Skill Python for Data Analysis.

Interviews will be via Microsoft Teams.

A reserve list may be held for a period up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made.

Important Dates

Eligibility checks from 23/09/2026 - 30/09/2026. Please be aware we will be sending all candidates an e-mail to complete a eligibility form.
Sift will be conducted from 01/10/2026
Interviews will be conducted from 13/10/2026

For the full terms and conditions of the post, please see attachment.

Please note that all campaigns may be subject to withdrawal at any stage if the internal resource position changes.

Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Security

Successful candidates must undergo a basic (or equivalent) criminal record check.

Successful candidates must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security needed is security check (opens in a new window).See our vetting charter (opens in a new window).

People working with government assets must complete baseline personnel security standard (opens in new window) checks.

Nationality requirements

This Job Is Broadly Open To The Following Groups

UK nationals
nationals of the Republic of Ireland

nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window)

Description

Duties Description

The Office of Strategic Planning and Innovation performs management activities designed to set priorities, focus energy and resources, strengthen operations, and ensure that employees and other stakeholders are working together to achieve measurable results. Duties

Under the direction of the Data Analyst 4, the Data Analyst 3 will be responsible for overseeing data and dashboard in the Office of Strategic Planning and Innovation within the Department of Civil Service. The Data Analyst 3 duties in Office of Strategic Planning and Innovation will include but are not limited to the following:

Manage staff in the development of reports for department executives and the Governor’s staff.
Collaborate with program administrators in the completion of agency wide reports.
Oversee staff in the development of the Department of Civil Service (DCS) strategic plan and monitoring associated metrics.
Provide business intelligence solutions for data in DCS Oracle and non-Oracle systems, such as NYSTEP, NYBEAS, StateJobs and ELMS and devise methods to identify data patterns and trends.
Research analytics tools and recommend solutions.
Validate that any predictive models provide accurate outcomes.
Identify proposed system changes that will impact data analysis efforts and propose solutions.
Direct staff in creating data sets, analyzing data and creating written reports.
Identify training needs and solutions for Data Analyst 2 and Data Analyst 1 staff.
Directly supervise a Data Analyst 2.

Non-competitve Qualifications

Nine years of experience in data visualization, statistical models and data mining tools.

Substitutions: An associate’s degree* may substitute for two years of general experience; or a bachelor’s degree may substitute for four years of general experience. A master’s degree* in data or computer science, informatics, economics, statistics, mathematics, or a related field, may substitute for one year of general experience; or a Ph.D.* in these fields may substitute for two years of general experience.

Your degree must have been awarded by a college or university accredited by a regional, national, or specialized agency recognized as an accrediting agency by the U.S. Department of Education/U.S. Secretary of Education. Current Department of Civil Service employees with one year of permanent, contingent permanent, or 55 B/C service as a Data Analyst 3.

About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Information security is an integral part of Visa's corporate culture. It is essential to maintain our position as an industry leader in electronic payments, which is why Visa has made it a priority to create top-tier security operations and incident response teams to defend the company against evolving cyber threats. If you would like to join a company where security is truly valued, where you can work with like-minded peers who are passionate about the art & science of cyber defense, and where you can use state of the art tools for maximum impact, then we have a home for you.

The successful candidate will work with a team of incident responders at one of Visa's Cyber Fusion Centers. The team is part of a larger organization located across multiple geographical sites that are responsible for the comprehensive cyber defense of Visa and its subsidiaries.

Essential Functions

Manage and address cybersecurity incidents through all stages, including identification, containment, and eradication.
Perform deep-dive analysis on systems, accounts, and networks to identify the root cause and impact of incidents.
Act as an engagement point for broader technology teams, including Cyber Defense and Engineering.
Perform proactive threat hunting to identify and mitigate potential threats before they can cause harm.
Develop and refine detection rules to improve the identification and response to security incidents.
Provide detailed reports and documentation of incidents and response actions.
Conduct quality control of the work performed by analysts to ensure accuracy and thoroughness.
Mentor and train junior analysts in advanced incident response techniques, tactics, and procedures.
Develop and maintain incident response playbooks and runbooks to ensure standardized and efficient response processes.
Contribute to identifying process improvement opportunities to enhance security incident response processes.
Implement process automation to streamline incident response workflows and improve efficiency.
Support and manage cybersecurity projects to enhance overall security posture.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

5+ years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 2 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 0 years of work experience with a PhD, OR 8+ years of relevant work experience.

Preferred Qualifications

6 or more years of work experience with a bachelor’s degree or 4 or more years of relevant experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or up to 3 years of relevant experience with a PhD.
Proven subject matter expertise in relevant areas, such as incident response, threat hunting, malware analysis, web application security or security engineering.
3+ years of Security Operations Center (SOC) work experience with a bachelor’s degree.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, or related technical discipline or equivalent professional experience related to Cybersecurity, Incident Response or information security.
Experience working in an enterprise-level incident response team or security operations center.
Relevant security-related certifications a plus: CISSP, GCIH, GCIA, GCED, GCFA, CySA+.
Demonstrated expertise in areas like incident response, intrusion and malware analysis, web application security, or security engineering.
Extensive understanding of malware types and network attack methods.
Strong grasp of TCP/IP, packet analysis, routing, and network security.
Extensive expertise in operating systems (Windows and Linux), as well as network services and applications.
Direct experience in handling cyber security incidents and associated incident response tools.
Strong working knowledge of common security tools such as SIEM, AV, WAF, IDS, Netflow, Packet Analyzer and Endpoint Detection & Response tools.
Understanding of web application security vulnerabilities, such as cross-site scripting, cross-site request forgery, SQL injection, denial-of-service attacks, and API attacks.
Good understanding of Web Application Security risks.
Excellent understanding of DDoS techniques and mitigation mechanisms.
Display great problem-solving skills, with tenacity and resilience to resolve issues.
Excellent communication and presentation skills with proven skill in presenting analytical data effectively to varied audiences.
Strong interpersonal and leadership skills to influence and build credibility as a peer.

jobs.description:
Proud to be 100% Canadian-owned, Northland Properties' are recognized as one of the most trusted names in hotels, restaurants, resorts, sports, construction, and asset management. Our well-known and loved brands have been bringing people together to celebrate unforgettable experiences across Canada, the US, Ireland, and the UK for over 50 years. As Canada’s fastest-growing hospitality group, we believe the foundation of our continued success is our people and their ability to take great care of our guests.

EMPLOYER:
Northland Properties Corporation (NPC)

LOCATION:
Support Centre, Vancouver, BC

EMPLOYMENT TYPE:
Full Time

COMPENSATION RANGE:
$60,000 - 80,000

BENEFITS:
Health/Dental/Vision, RRSP, Paid Time Off, Employee Perks.

Position Overview

The Security Analyst helps protect the Company’s technology environment, systems and information across Canada by monitoring security activity, investigating threats, supporting incident response and maintaining cybersecurity controls across corporate offices and operating locations.

Key Responsibilities

Monitor security alerts and suspicious activity across endpoints, networks, cloud services, identity platforms and business applications.
Triage and investigate cybersecurity incidents; escalate significant threats and support containment, recovery, documentation and lessons learned.
Administer and monitor security technologies, including endpoint detection and response, email security, vulnerability management, firewalls, multi-factor authentication and identity access controls.
Monitor Microsoft 365 and Azure security environments, including Entra ID, Microsoft Defender, Conditional Access, logging and alerting.
Perform vulnerability reviews and track remediation of critical patches, security updates and configuration issues.
Review user access, privileged accounts and security groups, including requirements for onboarding, role changes and departures.
Coordinate cybersecurity activities with internal IT teams, operating locations and managed service providers across Canada.
Support security assessments for new applications, vendors and technology changes.
Participate in phishing simulations, cybersecurity awareness initiatives and employee education.
Prepare reports on incidents, vulnerabilities, trends and risks, and maintain related procedures, technical documentation and system inventories.
Support business continuity, disaster recovery and cybersecurity incident response exercises.
Stay current on cybersecurity threats and recommend practical improvements.
Provide after-hours support during significant cybersecurity incidents when required.

Qualifications And Experience

Post-secondary education in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience.
Two to four years of experience in cybersecurity, IT security, systems administration, infrastructure or a related technical role.
Hands-on experience monitoring and investigating security alerts and incidents using security monitoring, endpoint detection, ticketing and vulnerability management tools.
Working knowledge of Windows, Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, networking fundamentals, identity and access management, endpoint security and vulnerability management.
Understanding of established cybersecurity practices and frameworks, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Controls and incident response lifecycle principles.
Experience supporting a geographically distributed, multi-site or 24-hour operating environment—particularly hospitality, retail or restaurants—is an asset.
Certifications such as Security+, CySA+, SC-200, SSCP or equivalent are assets.
Ability to handle confidential information with discretion, travel occasionally within Canada and provide after-hours support when required.

Capabilities

Analyzes security information methodically, exercises sound judgment and escalates issues appropriately.
Communicates technical information clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Maintains strong attention to detail and stays organized during competing priorities and security incidents.
Builds effective relationships with IT teams, business partners and external service providers.
Balances cybersecurity requirements with operational needs and recommends practical, risk-based solutions.
Takes ownership of assigned issues through resolution and continuously improves security processes and controls.

Measures of Success

Security alerts and incidents are reviewed, investigated, documented, escalated and resolved within established timelines.
Vulnerabilities and security gaps have clear remediation actions, owners and timelines.
User access and security controls are consistently reviewed and maintained.
IT teams and business partners receive timely, clear information during cybersecurity events.
Security procedures and documentation remain accurate and current.
Recurring security issues decrease through effective investigation, remediation and lessons learned.

Working Conditions

This Vancouver-based role supports locations across Canadian time zones in office and remote systems environments. Occasional travel and work outside normal business hours may be required during significant incidents, system changes or recovery activities.

jobs.description:
Job#: 3051817

Job Description:

Onsite in North Austin, TX

10-month contract

Job Description

A network security analyst ensures that information systems and computer networks are secure. This includes protecting the company against hackers and cyber-attacks, as well as monitoring network traffic and server logs for activity that seems unusual. Additionally, these analysts are responsible for finding vulnerabilities in the computer networks and creating recommendations for how to minimize these vulnerabilities. The network security analyst investigates security breaches, develops strategies for any security issues that arise, and utilizes the help of firewalls and antivirus software to maintain security.

Job Summary

The Network Security Analyst I performs advanced cybersecurity analysis and threat triage activities within the Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC). Work involves continuously monitoring, triaging, analyzing, and prioritizing cybersecurity alerts; investigating suspicious activity; identifying potential threats; and coordinating incident response activities to protect agency information systems, networks, and data. Serves as a primary point of contact for security event analysis, threat identification, and incident escalation.

Essential Job Functions

Monitors, analyzes, and triages cybersecurity alerts generated by Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), cloud security, email security, identity protection, and network security platforms.
Conducts initial investigations of detected and reported security events to determine severity, scope, impact, and potential risk to agency operations.
Identifies, validates, and prioritizes potential cybersecurity incidents, escalating confirmed threats to Incident Response, Threat Hunting, or SOC Engineering teams according to established procedures.
Correlates security events from multiple data sources, including endpoints (EDR), firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), intrusion prevention systems (IPS), cloud services, authentication systems, and threat intelligence feeds.
Reviews and analyzes indicators of compromise (IOCs), suspicious network activity, phishing emails, malware detections, and anomalous user behavior.
Documents investigations, findings, and response actions in ticketing and case management systems to ensure accurate tracking and reporting.
Assists with incident containment, eradication, and recovery efforts by coordinating with technical teams and stakeholders.
Reports and escalates to the CSOC Team Lead and/or SOC Manager.
Supports the continuous improvement of threat detection capabilities through alert tuning, process refinement, threat intelligence integration, and identification of false-positive trends.
Performs vulnerability assessment reviews and evaluates identified vulnerabilities for potential risk and remediation prioritization.
Supports development and maintenance of operational procedures, playbooks, workflows, and knowledge base articles related to threat detection and incident response.
Researches emerging cyber threats, attack techniques, tactics, and procedures (TTPs) to improve detection and response effectiveness.

jobs.description:
About FSA Federal

FSA Federal (FSA) provides professional services supporting law enforcement and homeland security missions across the United States.

The company is committed to delivering high-quality services to federal government customers and supporting initiatives that disrupt criminal organizations by identifying and removing the financial tools and proceeds associated with criminal activity.

FSA is seeking a Data Analyst to support the mission of the United States Attorney's Office (USAO), with a particular focus on asset forfeiture and case-related data management.

About the Role

FSA Federal is seeking a detail-oriented Data Analyst to provide data, documentation, and administrative support to the U.S. Attorney's Office.

In this role, you will collect, organize, analyze, reconcile, and accurately enter information from multiple sources. You will work with case files, databases, spreadsheets, legal and non-legal documents, reports, and correspondence, ensuring information is complete, accurate, properly formatted, and available when needed.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, meticulous, comfortable working with sensitive information, and able to manage multiple deadlines while maintaining a high standard of accuracy.

Receive, gather, analyze, and organize information from multiple sources.

Accurately enter required information into databases, documents, spreadsheets, and other systems.

Support the execution of the Compliance Testing and Monitoring program through data analysis, population identification and validation, sampling support, testing workbook preparation, results aggregation, and exception analysis.
Collect, validate, reconcile, and analyze data from internal systems, business reports, GRC tools, SharePoint, Excel workbooks, and other approved data sources used in compliance testing and monitoring activities.
Develop, maintain, document, and enhance compliance testing methodologies and analytics routines, including data logic, testing rules, exception criteria, thresholds, sampling logic, repeatable queries, and testing outputs.
Develop and maintain testing data files, dashboards, metrics, reports, trackers, and recurring monitoring routines to support timely, accurate, and consistent testing execution and reporting.
Develop and enhance automated and semi-automated testing, monitoring, and reporting solutions using tools such as Excel, Power BI, Power Automate, SharePoint, SQL, and other approved analytics, reporting, or workflow tools.
Analyze large data populations to identify trends, outliers, anomalies, potential exceptions, repeat issues, control weaknesses, and emerging compliance risks.
Support risk-based testing by translating test objectives into data requirements, identifying relevant populations and testing attributes, supporting sample selection, and validating the completeness and reliability of data used for testing.
Prepare clear and accurate testing results summaries, exception reports, trend analyses, dashboards, metrics, and management reporting that communicate testing outcomes, risk themes, identified issues, and remediation status.
Support testing execution and workpaper quality by preparing and maintaining accurate, complete, organized, and independently reviewable data extracts, sampling files, calculations, evidence, supporting documentation, exception validation, and testing results.
Assist Compliance Testing team members with data preparation, exception validation, evidence gathering, issue documentation, root cause analysis support, remediation validation, and retesting activities.
Maintain testing-related schedules, trackers, reporting inventories, issue validation logs, action item logs, and documentation repositories to support effective program governance, transparency, and timely completion of testing activities.
Partner with Compliance, Legal, Risk, Audit, IT, Data, and Business Unit stakeholders to obtain data, clarify data definitions and requirements, resolve data quality issues, and support timely completion of testing and monitoring activities.
Support compliance testing reporting and data requests for the Chief Compliance Officer, senior management, management committees, bank partners, audits, examinations, regulators, and other oversight stakeholders.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve testing efficiency, reporting consistency, data quality, automation, monitoring routines, documentation, and repeatability of testing processes.
Support special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

Experience analyzing and reconciling large data populations, identifying trends and anomalies, and preparing accurate reporting required.
Advanced Excel skills required; experience with SQL, Power BI, Power Automate, SharePoint, GRC systems, or similar tools preferred.
Experience with testing methodologies, monitoring logic, exception rules, sampling methodologies, or repeatable analytics routines preferred.
General understanding of compliance testing, internal controls, issue validation, documentation standards, and consumer financial services compliance preferred.
Strong analytical, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to translate testing objectives into data requirements, analyze results, prepare clear reporting, and maintain accurate and independently reviewable documentation while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
Ability to collaborate effectively across Compliance, Legal, IT, Data, and Business Unit stakeholders.
Demonstrated sound judgment, discretion, professionalism, and ability to handle confidential information in a fast-paced environment.

This position is an office-based position where you must be able to sit for long periods of time. The employee will be working on a computer 90% of the time.

jobs.title: Credit Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Credit views on this bank's covered issuers currently rely on periodic reviews that go stale between rating cycles, and a global bank standing up its India technology and operations centre has partnered with Flexiple to hire a Credit Research Analyst who will keep those views current on its India credit research desk.
The desk you'd support

This desk covers a portfolio of corporate and financial issuers, tracking their credit profile, capital structure and covenant headroom, and feeding that analysis into the rating views and internal credit opinions used across lending, trading and risk functions. The work sits close to real decisions: a stale credit view here can show up as a mispriced position or a missed covenant breach somewhere else in the bank.
How a rating call gets made

Building and maintaining financial models for covered issuers, including leverage, coverage and liquidity metrics
Tracking covenant compliance, rating actions and credit events across the assigned portfolio
Drafting credit notes and issuer updates that summarise financial performance against thesis and triggers
Supporting senior analysts on new issuer onboarding, including first-pass credit write-ups
Monitoring macro, sector and regulatory developments that could move an issuer's credit profile

What we're looking for in a first read

2 to 6 years of experience in credit research, corporate ratings, fixed income research or related credit analysis, with strong financial modelling skills and comfort reading financial statements, indentures and credit agreements. You should be able to write a credit note that a senior analyst can sign off on with minimal rework, and be precise about assumptions in a leverage or coverage model.
Where the seat sits

The role is based out of Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Hyderabad or Pune, or Remote (India), working alongside a global credit research function with regular touchpoints across time zones.
After you apply

The process includes an HR Screening, a modelling or case assignment, a Technical Round with the credit team and a final Culture Fit conversation. One application here covers this opening and any other Flexiple-matched role that fits your experience, so there is no need to reapply.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Sponsorship:
GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H-1B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.)

Remote:
This role is categorized as remote. This means the successful candidate may be based anywhere in the United States and is not expected to report to a GM worksite unless directed by their manager.

The Role:

The Business Analyst – Zero Waste, Chemical, & Resource Management (SP2) provides analytical and operational support to GM’s global Zero Waste, Resource Management (RM), Chemical Management (CM), and biological control programs. This role enables data-driven decision making, effective budget management, and disciplined execution to enable the SP2 team to advance GM’s environmental, safety, and cost-optimization objectives.

The analyst partners closely with SP2 program leads, plant teams, Infrastructure & Corporate Citizenship (ICC), Procurement, Finance, EH&S, and external suppliers to ensure goals are set, tracked, and achieved across North America and globally

What You'll Do (Responsibilities):

Zero Waste program support

Support development, alignment, and annual refresh of global Zero Waste goals, targets, and roadmaps for SP2 programs.
Maintain dashboards and scorecards for Zero Waste performance (e.g., waste generation, diversion, recovery, and cost metrics) at plant, regional, and enterprise levels.
Track progress against site-level action plans, escalate gaps, and highlight best practices and high-performing sites.
Coordinate recurring Zero Waste governance routines (cadence, agendas, pre-read materials, action item tracking, and follow-up).

Resource Management (RM) and Chemical Management (CM) financial support

Support development of annual RM and CM budgets for US and Canada, including volume, rate, and savings assumptions.
Build and maintain budget tracking tools that connect forecasts, actuals, and variances at the program, supplier, and site levels.
Coordinate purchase order (PO) requests, shopping carts, and change requests for RM, CM, and related environmental services, ensuring alignment with budget and contracts.
Monitor PO status, goods receipts, and invoice issues; work with Finance, Procurement, and suppliers to resolve discrepancies.
Provide periodic and ad hoc spend analysis, including cost drivers, savings realization, and scenario analysis.

Zero Waste and Environmental Capex support

Support Zero Waste and related environmental capex planning by compiling site requests, business cases, and benefit estimates.
Track approval status, spend, and realized benefits of capex projects (e.g., equipment for waste reduction, segregation, logistics, and treatment).
Maintain a portfolio view of Zero Waste and environmental investments, including timing, risks, and interdependencies.

Biological control of Metal Removal Fluids (MRF) and Metal Removal Fluids Strategy Team (MRFST) support

Support SP2’s biological control responsibilities for MRF and MRFST, including program documentation, data collection, and routine reporting.
Coordinate with plants, vendors, and technical experts to monitor performance (e.g., treatment effectiveness, volumes, quality parameters, and operational issues).
Help identify optimization opportunities in dosing, equipment, logistics, and supplier performance to improve safety, reliability, and total cost.

Data, analytics, and insights

Analyze RM and CM safety incidents, near misses, and risk identifications to detect patterns, “read across” opportunities, and common tasks with elevated risk.
Develop visualizations and summaries that translate complex data into clear insights and recommendations for SP2 leadership and stakeholders.
Maintain and continuously improve standard reports, dashboards, and tools (e.g., in Excel, Power BI, or other GM-approved platforms).
Aggregate and analyze waste, recycling, and diversion data (volumes, materials, destinations, costs, and rebates) across sites to identify trends, outliers, and improvement opportunities.

Industry trends, technology, and benchmarking

Monitor external trends in waste reduction, waste handling and logistics, biological treatment, and chemical selection for indirect materials.
Summarize industry developments, regulatory changes, and emerging technologies with potential impact on GM’s Zero Waste, RM, and CM strategies.
Support pilots and evaluations of new technologies or service models, including data collection, KPI design, and results reporting.
Provide structured benchmarking against peer companies and best-in-class service models where data is available.

Governance, processes, and documentation

Maintain organized, current documentation for SP2 programs (standards, procedures, playbooks, training content, meeting notes, and decision logs).
Support development and refinement of common processes, templates, and tools for Zero Waste, RM, CM, and biological control.
Help ensure alignment with GM safety, compliance, and information management requirements in all SP2 program artifacts.
Coordinate cross-functional working sessions, workshops, and knowledge-sharing forums to disseminate lessons learned and best practices.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)
:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business, Data Analytics, or related fields
5+ years of experience in business analysis, data analytics, operations, EH&S, environmental programs, or related discipline.
Demonstrated experience with data analysis and reporting (Microsoft Excel; experience with tools such as Power BI or similar is a plus).
Experience supporting budgets, forecasts, or financial tracking (e.g., spend, variance analysis, savings tracking); familiarity with enterprise systems for POs and invoices (e.g., SAP or equivalent).
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills with the ability to work with large datasets and multiple systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to summarize complex topics and influence stakeholders at different levels.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and follow through on commitments with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

What Can Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

Experience in waste management, resource management, chemical management, environmental engineering, or industrial operations.
Familiarity with Zero Waste concepts, waste hierarchy, and recycling/landfill diversion strategies.
Experience working with safety data (incidents, near misses, risk assessments) and translating insights into practical risk-reduction actions.
Knowledge of biological treatment or biological control applications in material recovery, wastewater, or related environmental systems.
Experience working with manufacturing plants, logistics providers, and/or environmental service suppliers.
Demonstrated ability to develop or improve business processes, templates, and governance routines.

What is the Opportunity?

Aecon U.S. requires a dedicated Procurement Business Analyst to convert fragmented procure-to-pay and project data into a reliable management system for EPC delivery. The role provides the analytical capacity, KPI ownership, reporting automation, and control visibility needed to identify cost, schedule, funding, vendor, invoice, and compliance risks before they affect project outcomes. This is an enabling role for Procurement Leadership and project teams, not a transactional buying position, and will create repeatable tools and standards that scale across the U.S. EPC portfolio.

What You'll Do Here

Procurement Analytics and Reporting

Own and continuously improve executive-ready EPC procurement dashboards, scorecards, and reporting in Power BI and Excel, with clear definitions, accountable data owners, and documented refresh cycles.
Analyze spend, commitments, purchase orders, invoices, vendors, funding, periods of performance, cycle times, and closeout status to identify leakage, bottlenecks, savings opportunities, and cost or schedule exposure.
Provide recurring operating reviews and decision-focused analysis for Procurement Leadership, EPC project teams, Finance, Accounts Payable, Commercial, and executive stakeholders.
Establish and maintain a governed KPI framework covering sourcing pipeline, purchase-order cycle time, commitment coverage, invoice exceptions, vendor performance, funding utilization, open obligations, and closeout readiness.

Business Analysis and Process Improvement

Partner with stakeholders to define, validate, prioritize, and document business requirements, reporting needs, control gaps, and improvement opportunities across the EPC procure-to-pay lifecycle.
Translate business needs into practical data models, dashboards, process maps, controls, workflows, and operating procedures with clear ownership and acceptance criteria.
Perform root-cause and exception analysis; quantify business impact; and recommend corrective actions for procurement, invoice, vendor, funding, data-quality, and operational issues.
Support future-state process design, procurement transformation, change adoption, governance, audit readiness, corrective-action tracking, and continuous improvement.

Data Management and Business Intelligence

Extract, validate, cleanse, reconcile, and integrate procurement and project data from SAP and other approved enterprise sources, maintaining traceability to source records.
Develop maintainable Power BI data models, calculations, measures, visualizations, and executive dashboards that support drill-down from portfolio trends to actionable exceptions.
Use advanced Excel, PivotTables, Power Query, Power Pivot, lookup functions, data models, dashboards, and validation controls to automate repeatable analysis and reduce manual reporting effort.
Maintain data dictionaries, KPI and calculation logic, report inventories, ownership, refresh schedules, and standardized practices; monitor and resolve data-quality issues.

Procurement Performance and Support

Monitor commitments, purchase orders, vendor performance, invoice exceptions, open obligations, periods of performance, funding utilization, change exposure, and closeout status; escalate material exceptions with recommended actions.
Deliver spend, demand, and market analysis to support sourcing strategy, vendor management, budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow visibility, and procurement planning for EPC work.
Develop quantitative vendor and procurement performance measures, track action closure, and communicate findings, risks, and recommendations to technical, operational, commercial, and executive audiences.

Required Qualifications

What You Bring to the Team:

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Data Analytics, Economics, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
At least 3 years of directly relevant analytical experience; 5 to 7 years of progressively responsible experience preferred, ideally supporting project-based or capital-intensive operations.
Advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI capability, plus experience extracting and reconciling data from SAP or another enterprise resource planning platform.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, validate data, quantify business impact, communicate with executives, and drive cross-functional actions to closure.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in EPC, construction, engineering, industrial, nuclear, energy, federal contracting, or another regulated, project-driven environment.

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Here at the Office for National Statistics (ONS), we have unrivalled access to a vast breadth and depth of data. Every day, we use this to produce trusted statistics and insightful analysis that informs both the public and policymakers on the issues that matter most.

Our work spans the production of essential economic statistics and the analysis that brings them to life to support decision makers and help people understand the UK economy. Our key focus is producing high quality, relevant and timely core statistics: gross domestic product, inflation, public sector finances, labour market statistics, trade and the balance of payments. We're also expanding our use of administrative data, while transforming our surveys and moving off legacy statistical systems.

Following the recent independent review of ONS by Sir Robert Devereux, we’ve launched our Economic Statistics Plan (ESP)—a bold response to restore quality and confidence in our economic statistics. The plan outlines how we assess the quality of our core outputs, the steps we’re taking to address risks and challenges, and the foundations we’re laying for the future. These changes will help us build a more resilient statistical system that supports confident decision-making and a clearer understanding of UK society.

Delivering the ESP successfully requires a collective effort. As part of that, ONS is recruiting a number of Data Analysts to help us understand, manipulate, and accurately analyse data—providing insight that informs both internal and external audiences. You will play a key role in delivering the Plan, and in developing our people, building good working relationships across the organisation and making ONS a great place to work.

We’re particularly interested to hear from applicants with experience with economic data sources, such as business surveys; or a background in economics, finance, or accountancy.

Job Description

Data analysts collect, organise and study data to provide business and operational insight. They work across a broad range of areas and topics.

Data analysts understand, manipulate and accurately analyse data to provide insight about a topic for internal and external audiences. They make complex topics easier for everyone to understand, including non-specialist audiences.

Key Responsibilities Of Data Analysts Include

manage, clean, abstract and aggregate data alongside a range of analytical studies on that data
identify, collect and migrate data to and from a range of systems
manipulate and link different data sets
help with data quality checking and cleaning
use tools and techniques for data analysis, data visualisation and provision of business insight
present data and conclusions logically and concisely in the most appropriate format, while following the Analysis Function standards
summarise and present the results of data analysis to a range of customers — this includes making recommendations for how to use the data
interpret and apply relevant data information security standards, policies and procedures to data
perform routine statistical analysis and answer queries, which may include the production of reports
use a range of analytical techniques such as data mining, time series, forecasting and modelling techniques to identify and predict trends in data
work with data architecture
use coding and programming skills for data and analytics

Please note we will not be badging to an analytical profession as part of this campaign. However, there are regular opportunities for staff to apply for badging with the relevant government analytical profession upon joining ONS.

Person specification

Essential Criteria -

Data Analysis (Lead Criterion): Ability to interpret and work with diverse data sets, identifying trends, resolving issues, and using programming tools to analyse and assure data quality.
Effective Communication: Ability to identify and clearly communicate trends, insights, and anomalies in data to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leaders.
Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration: Demonstrable ability to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders, building strong working relationships to support shared objectives.

Qualifications

We welcome applications from individuals who satisfy the essential criteria and are a member of, or eligible to join, one of eligibility for the government analytical professions as listed below :

Government Economic Service (GES),
Government Statistical Service (GSS),
Government Operational Research Service (GORS), or
Government Social Research (GSR).

To achieve this, candidates need to hold at least;

A 2.2 degree in economics, OR
A 2.2 in a social science related subject with sufficient research OR
A 2:2 in a numerate subject containing taught statistical content

OR

A minimum 2 years relevant work experience

Please note - All candidates are expected to ensure they meet the entry requirements. Failure to demonstrate how you meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Making Effective Decisions
Communicating and Influencing
Working Together

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

Data Quality - Understands and can explain statistical / research methods and the differences between sources, such as concepts or different data sets. Is able to design and choose best methods for data collection.
Analysis Approach - Utilises analytical tools to analyse data for trends and gaps, applying approved techniques to create coherent series’ and data modelling
Presentation / Dissemination - Communicates in a straightforward and engaging manner, choosing appropriate styles to maximise understanding.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £34,587, Office for National Statistics contributes £10,019 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our 5400 valued colleagues across the business.

Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that the benefits pack attached (bottom of page)
will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture.

Inclusion & Accessibility

At ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.

If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

and the department will consider eligibility by exception on a case-by-case basis. You will be asked to provide information regarding your UK residency during your application, and failure to provide this will result in your application being rejected.

At the point of SC application, you will need to provide or give access to the following evidence:
