In 14 of our 18 geographies, we lead the category in terms of customers served and we continue to gain market share. We have a strong track record of profitable and resilient growth, primarily delivered organically by our codified and industrialised business model with high share of recurring revenues (about 90%) and industry leading retention.

Our mission is to give our customers peace of mind by protecting what matters most to them. We believe that everyone has the right to feel safe and secure.

For the year ended 31 December 2025, Verisure delivered another year of strong, profitable growth, generating €3.7 billion in Total Revenue, €1.7 billion in Adjusted EBITDA (46% margin) and €953 million in Adjusted EBIT (25% margin). For more information:  www.verisure.com

Verisure in the Nordics

Born in Sweden over 35 years ago, Verisure has grown from a local pioneer into the leading provider of monitored security solutions across the Nordic region and globally.
Today, Sweden stands as our third largest market and Norway as our fifth, with Denmark and Finland playing critical strategic roles in our portfolio. All four countries have delivered exceptional growth over the past five years and hold #1 positions in their respective markets.

With more than 2,000 passionate colleagues and partners across the Nordics, we proudly protect homes and small businesses every day.
As we continue to scale and accelerate, strengthening our brand, reputation, and trust with customers, communities, and key stakeholders is essential. Our ambition is clear: to make the Nordics the most recognized and most preferred security provider in the region.

Responsibilities Of The Corporate Security Manager

As Nordic Security Manager, you hold full accountability for the Corporate Security function across the Nordic region, with a clear mandate to lead, shape, and continuously strengthen the overall security framework
. You are expected to define and drive the regional security strategy, ensuring it is not only aligned with global standards but also effectively translated into concrete actions, measurable outcomes, and consistent execution across all Nordic markets.

In this role, you are not only responsible for setting direction—you are expected to ensure delivery, follow-through, and tangible impact
. You will proactively identify risks, challenge existing ways of working, and implement robust frameworks that enhance resilience, protect critical assets, and support the business in achieving its strategic objectives.

You will operate in a highly cross-functional environment, working closely with senior stakeholders across Legal, HR, Technology, Information Security, and Compliance. As a trusted partner, you are expected to influence decision-making at a senior level, provide clear and actionable insights, and ensure that security is embedded into business processes rather than treated as a standalone function
. In parallel, you will collaborate with international peers and Group functions to drive consistency, share best practices, and contribute to the continuous evolution of the global security agenda.

Success in this role requires the ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on involvement
, taking ownership in critical situations while maintaining a long-term, proactive perspective on risk and security development.

Core responsibilities

Develop and implement the corporate and physical security strategy across the Nordic region, ensuring a consistent level of security maturity across all markets to protect Verisure’s people, facilities, assets, operations, information, reputation, service continuity, and customer trust against risks of any nature
Identify risks, gaps, threats, and vulnerabilities, and drive preventive, reactive, and predictive mitigation actions
Lead internal investigations focused on the detection and prevention of misconduct fraud, loss of sensitive information, illegal competition, and other security-related irregularities
Address internal and external incidents with potential legal, operational, financial, or reputational impact, ensuring appropriate investigation, escalation, documentation, and follow-through
Collaborate with HR, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Technology, and Information Security to gather relevant evidence, support sensitive investigations, and ensure actions are aligned with company policies and applicable requirements
Coordinate, where appropriate, with law enforcement, public authorities, external advisors, and relevant security bodies in connection with incidents or investigations
Develop preventive and predictive methodologies to strengthen fraud deterrence, crime prevention, and loss prevention across the region
Monitor compliance with security policies, procedures, standards, and governance requirements, including alignment with global standards and regulatory expectations
Promote employee awareness, responsible behaviours, and a strong security and compliance culture across the Nordics
Lead corporate security initiatives, including insider risk, personnel security, physical security, crime prevention, fraud deterrence, and investigations
Prevent, detect, manage, and learn from security incidents with potential operational, legal, financial, or reputational impact
Own and continuously improve incident management processes, tools, reporting routines, and governance across the region
Provide intelligence, analysis, and actionable insights related to incidents, investigations, risks, and emerging threats to support strategic decision-making
Define, track, and report security KPIs and continuous improvement metrics, including investigation, fraud, incident, and resilience indicators
Own and develop the Nordic Business Continuity Planning framework, ensuring readiness to protect critical services and recover effectively from disruption
Lead crisis management processes, coordination, exercises, and continuous improvement, ensuring the organisation can respond with structure, speed, and discipline
Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership across the Nordics, translating complex security risks into clear, pragmatic, and business-oriented recommendations
Collaborate with Group and regional security leaders to share best practices, drive consistency, and contribute to the evolution of Verisure’s broader security agenda
Contribute to enterprise risk management, organisational resilience, and the safe development of the business across the Nordic region

Candidate profile

You are a highly seasoned and trusted security leader with the ability to operate confidently at both strategic and operational levels in a complex, international environment. With a strong track record of leading security functions across multiple countries, you bring deep expertise across corporate security, physical security, personnel security, fraud deterrence, investigations, business continuity, crisis management, and organisational resilience.

You understand that security is not only about protecting the business from risk, but also about enabling the business to grow in a safe, trusted, and disciplined way. You have a well-developed business mindset and understand how to balance risk, operational needs, customer trust, reputation, and commercial priorities, while maintaining the highest standards of integrity and professionalism. You are a natural influencer who builds credibility quickly with senior stakeholders and can translate complex security risks into clear, actionable business decisions. Known for your sound judgment and discretion, you are comfortable handling sensitive matters, working with confidential information, and navigating high-pressure situations with calm, structure, and follow-through. You combine analytical depth with a strong execution mindset and have a proven ability to develop preventive and predictive approaches, implement frameworks, lead investigations, manage incidents, and continuously strengthen security maturity across markets.

Experience And Qualifications

new_jobs.title: Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Location:

4910 Tiedeman Road, Brooklyn Ohio

Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst

Position Summary

Our Cyber Threat Management team is part of Key's broader Cyber Defense function within Corporate Information Security. Cyber Defense's mission is simple: We aim to Deter, Detect, Deny, and Disrupt adversaries through proactive threat-centric defense.

This senior strategic role advances KeyBank's Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) program by converting external and internal threat information into forward looking intelligence that informs business decisions, cybersecurity strategy, control investments, and enterprise risk management. The analyst will maintain and refine intelligence requirements, assess the financial services threat landscape, and evaluate geopolitical developments and emerging technology risks that may affect KeyBank, its customers, its third-party ecosystem, and its long-term objectives.

The analyst will produce strategic forecasts, control gap assessments, executive level intelligence products, and decision support for senior leaders. The role will also support briefings for the Board and regulators, translate complex threats into clear business impact, and help leaders prioritize resources based on intelligence, exposure, and risk. Success requires strong judgment, research, writing, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to deliver accurate, concise, and complete assessments.

Key Responsibilities

Aggregate, evaluate, and synthesize threat intelligence from diverse sources such as open-source intelligence (OSINT), dark web forums, commercial feeds, and internal sources to identify relevant and actionable strategic insights for the organization.
Strategic Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Report Writing & Briefing - Produce forward looking assessments, executive summaries and strategic forecasts on adversaries, campaigns, geopolitical developments, regulatory concerns, and technology driven risks.
Establish feedback measures that assess whether intelligence products are timely, relevant, actionable, and aligned to stakeholder needs.
Analyze the financial services industry threat landscape, including threats to banking operations, customers, payments, third parties, critical infrastructure, and sector confidence.
Evaluate emerging technology risks involving technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud services, quantum computing).
Deep understanding of Threat Actor (TA) Tactics, Techniques, & Procedures (TTPs) and Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) utilized by cyber adversaries with the ability to identify new and novel TTP’s.
Provide intelligence support during significant incidents or emerging threat events by clarifying context, likely implications, and potential future developments.
Conduct threat to control gap assessments by comparing relevant adversary capabilities and attack paths with existing security controls, risk treatments, and business dependencies.
Familiarity with leveraging frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, D3FEND, Diamond Model, Kill Chain), security platforms like Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR), Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP), and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR).
Apply intelligence led prioritization to help focus defensive resources, control improvements, threat hunting, vulnerability management, exercises (tabletop, red / blue / purple), and risk decisions on the threats most relevant to KeyBank.
Partner with Cyber Defense, Security Engineering, Fraud, Third-Party Risk Management, Third-Party Security, Technology, Legal, and other teams to assess and communicate cyber risks.
Provide mentorship and technical guidance to junior analysts and cross functional partners.
Lead by example in fostering a culture of curiosity, rigor, and continuous learning within the CTI function.
Represent KeyBank within intelligence sharing communities, industry working groups, government partnerships, and peer collaboration forums.
Leverage external partnerships and intelligence exchanges to strengthen organizational awareness and preparedness.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field—or equivalent experience
5+ years in CTI.
Demonstrated experience managing intelligence requirements and producing strategic intelligence for senior decision makers.
Strong understanding of the financial services threat environment and the business, operational, customer, third-party, and regulatory impacts of cyber threats.
Experience assessing geopolitical risk, state-sponsored activity, and emerging technology risks in a business or security context.
Ability to connect threat information to security controls, business exposure, and risk-based priorities.
Strong analytical, research, and writing skills.
Ability to work independently and escalate risks appropriately.
Ability to communicate concisely, effectively and directly with executive management.

Preferred Certifications

GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI)
Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+)
CompTIA Security+

Compensation And Benefits

This position is eligible to earn a base salary in the range of $96,000.00 - $181,000.00 annually. Placement within the pay range may differ based upon various factors, including but not limited to skills, experience and geographic location. Compensation for this role also includes eligibility for incentive compensation which may include production, commission, and/or discretionary incentives.

Please click here for a list of benefits for which this position is eligible.

Crisis24 is a global, AI-enhanced provider of travel risk management, mass communications, critical event management, crisis-security consulting, personal protection solutions and global medical concierge capabilities, allowing prominent organizations, disruptive brands and influential people to operate with confidence in an uncertain world. Backed by proprietary AI-enabled SaaS technologies, advanced Global Operations Centers, an extensive global footprint, and the largest team of private-sector intelligence analysts in the world, we deliver localized insights and global perspectives alongside medical, security, crisis response, embedded intelligence, and consultancy services as a preferred partner for Fortune 500 corporations.

At Crisis24, we don't just offer jobs – we offer missions. We recruit the very best from the military, intelligence agencies, academia, law enforcement, medicine, or any of our areas of specialty. We protect more than places. We protect people, reputations, and lifestyles, with integrity, discipline, discretion, and purpose. Whether you're stepping into civilian life after service, seeking personal or professional growth, or bringing specialized expertise to a higher calling, we match your ambition with real opportunity. Do the most important work of your career, helping safeguard the world's most important organizations and individuals against risk.

More information is available at https://www.crisis24.com/careers

Essential Duties/Responsibilities

Support the core functions of the client’s 24/7/365 Global Security Operations Center (GSOC). The GSOC analyst monitors and responds to security threats across the client’s global operations.

The analyst will work in the GSOC located at the client’s office in Colorado Springs, Colorado.

The analyst is expected to perform shiftwork (including nights, evenings, weekends, and holidays) to meet the 24/7/365 needs of the GSOC.

Analysts will assess alerts and incidents for client impact, assist in producing specific briefings or presentations, manage emergency incidents using judgment and skills in accordance with commonly accepted incident management best practices and client policies and procedures, and perform other duties as assigned within the scope of the program.

This is not a cyber security or data analysis position.

What You Will Bring

Bachelor’s degree required
1 to 3 years of experience in intelligence gathering, analysis, alerting, threat assessment, incident response, or a related field required.
Ability to take initiative and multitask under pressure.
Ability to intake, evaluate, and sift large quantities of information.
Effective problem-solving, time management, and analytical skills.
Knowledge of world news and current events.
Strong written and verbal communication skills required, including accurate typing skills.
Knowledge of Microsoft Office, especially Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Knowledge of Google Earth and Maps or other Geographic Information System platforms.
Strong customer-service skills, especially in person and over the phone; ability to communicate across varying professional levels.
Familiarity with security tools, incident monitoring tools, and incident response procedures is preferred. Foreign travel and experience preferred.

Data Protection

Adhere to applicable information security procedures and policies as updated from time to time on the ISMS. Report any information security incidents or potential information security threats to the Information Security Officer. Take a proactive approach to information security.

Information Security

Protect the data and systems of Crisis24 and its stakeholders by adhering to policies, reporting incidents and potential problems, completing regular training, and identifying opportunities for improvement.

new_jobs.description:
As Data Analyst, USCA Transportation,
you are responsible for supporting transportation and logistics operations through data analysis, performance measurement, reporting, and business intelligence initiatives. You serve as a key analytical resource supporting logistics transformation, transportation operations, carrier management, network optimization, and continuous improvement efforts. You collaborate with stakeholders across various functions within PPG to develop actionable insights, identify improvement opportunities, and support strategic decision-making through data-driven analysis. You will work out of the Corporate HQ office in Pittsburgh and report to the Associate Director, Logistics Operations & Planning.

Responsibilities

Analyze transportation performance, freight spend, service levels, network flows, and operational efficiency to identify trends, risks, root causes, and improvement opportunities across all transportation modes.
Develop, maintain, and enhance transportation dashboards, scorecards, KPI reporting, and business intelligence tools that support operational and executive decision-making.
Ensure data integrity, reporting accuracy, and consistency across transportation systems, ERP platforms, and reporting solutions while supporting data governance and quality improvement initiatives.
Provide analytical support for carrier management, transportation sourcing events, bid analyses, contract reviews, and performance measurement against cost and service objectives.
Support transportation network optimization, route design, shipment consolidation, modeling, and other initiatives that improve service, efficiency, and total logistics cost.
Participate in logistics transformation projects and digital solution initiatives by supporting system implementation, testing, validation, adoption, continuous improvement, and project execution activities.
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders across Supply Chain, Operations, Procurement, Finance, IT, and Commercial teams to communicate insights, present recommendations, drive process improvements, and measure realized business benefits.

Requirements

BS/BA degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Information Systems, or related field.
(3+) years of experience in transportation, logistics, supply chain analytics, business intelligence, or related analytical roles.
Advanced Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization platforms.
Experience working with Transportation Management Systems (OTM, SAP TM, Blue Yonder, or equivalent).
Knowledge of SQL, database reporting tools, and data analytics methodologies.
Understanding of transportation operations, freight management, and supply chain processes.
Experience with logistics network modeling and transportation optimization tools is preferred.

Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Data Analyst to join our Business Data Operations Division.

Business Data Operations Division (BDOD) is a large and diverse area of around 400 staff, collecting economic statistics from several million businesses a year. It is the foundation for most of the ONS’ core economic outputs, such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The primary role for the division is the data collection, editing and validation of survey data.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social, and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.

Job Description

A Data Analyst collects, organises and studies data to provide business insight.

Responsibilities Include

Build analytical pipelines for automated processing of data used for regular reporting.
Lead the production of regular data and insight products.
Lead on the development and delivery of robust quality control processes over our outputs including the use of automated tests to validate processing.
Design and build creative data visualisations to deliver actionable insights for our business users.
Lead on the development of Power BI data models
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to collect information to support the measurement of ONS performance e.g. KPIs, monthly, quarterly, and annual reports etc used to track ONS performance.
Lead the delivery of management information products, liaising with stakeholders and collecting user requirements.
Lead the development of system and user process documentation; developing new documentation as required and updates to existing documentation.
Line manage, develop and coach 1-2 Data Analysts within your team.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

Applying statistical and analytical tools and techniques
(Practitioner)

lead the development of valuable statistical and analytical insights and reports
identify and apply a range of statistical and analytical techniques and tools, and support others in applying them
quality assure statistical techniques and analytical outputs across a team
engage with stakeholders and share statistical and analytical techniques to increase understanding and trust

Developing code for analysis
(Practitioner)

design and implement the analytical approach, including code, using appropriate standards and tests
lead collaboration to review and improve analytical approaches, including shared code
guide others in producing analytical approach documentation, identifying improvements

Communicating between the technical and non-technical
(Practitioner)

listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations
manage active and reactive communication
support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

Data visualisation
(Practitioner)

use a range of data visualisations to simplify a complex story.
adapt a story to the needs of multidisciplinary stakeholders.
advise and support others in developing inclusive, accessible data visualisations that recognise different user needs.
suggest improvements to data visualisation processes and standards to increase efficiency and quality.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Communicating and Influencing
Making Effective Decisions
Working Together
Leadership

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

Python for Data Analysis

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £41,985, Office for National Statistics contributes £12,163 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our valued colleagues across the organisation.

Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that our careers site will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture.

Inclusion & Accessibility

At ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.

If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Experience and Technical skills.

Security Clearance

For ONS the requirement for SC clearance is to have been present in the UK for 3 consecutive years immediately prior to applying
and the department will consider eligibility by exception on a case-by-case basis. You will be asked to provide information regarding your UK residency during your application, and failure to provide this will result in your application being rejected.

At the point of SC application, you will need to provide or give access to the following evidence:

Departmental or company records (personnel files, staff reports, sick leave reports and security records)
UK criminal records covering both spent and unspent criminal records
Your credit and financial history with a credit reference agency
Security Services records

Please note: We will reach out to you once the advert has closed to confirm eligibility for this role, this will be via an e-mail. Please check you e-mails.

ONS are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants are expected to hold a valid right to work in the UK when employment commences. If you are applying on a time-limited visa, this will need to be valid for at least 18 months at point of application.

To work at the ONS, candidates must meet both UK right to work and security clearance requirements (where applicable).

If you are unsure whether you meet the appropriate right to work or security clearance eligibility criteria, please refer to the guidance on Gov.uk or contact the recruitment email provided in the advert before applying
. Failure to meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected and employment offers being withdrawn.

Application Process

Number of Stages: 2

Stage 1: Application

Stage 2: Interview

Stage 1 – Application

The assessment process at the application stage will be based on your work history, CV, skills, experience, and personal statement. It is important that your application is tailored to highlight the skills, knowledge, and experience relevant to the role.

A personal statement is required at application stage, the maximum word count allowed is 1,250 words, which should not be exceeded. You should provide evidence for each essential skill criterion listed in the person specification. As these criteria are scored, it is advisable to give clear examples for each one, including the impact of your actions, ideally utilising the STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

In instances where a high number of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted, and candidates will be invited to interview based on merit order, i.e., those with the highest scores.

Stage 2
– Interview

If invited to interview, you will be assessed using techniques aligned with the Civil Service Success Profiles framework, covering all behaviours listed in the job advert and any required technical skills.

You will be required to provide a 5 minute presentation at interview. The presentation topic will be emailed to candidates who have passed the initial online application stage, 1 week prior to interview. This presentation will assess candidates against the Technical Skill Python for Data Analysis.

Interviews will be via Microsoft Teams.

A reserve list may be held for a period up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made.

People working with government assets must complete baseline personnel security standard (opens in new window) checks.

Job Description:

Onsite in North Austin, TX

10-month contract

Job Description

A network security analyst ensures that information systems and computer networks are secure. This includes protecting the company against hackers and cyber-attacks, as well as monitoring network traffic and server logs for activity that seems unusual. Additionally, these analysts are responsible for finding vulnerabilities in the computer networks and creating recommendations for how to minimize these vulnerabilities. The network security analyst investigates security breaches, develops strategies for any security issues that arise, and utilizes the help of firewalls and antivirus software to maintain security.

Job Summary

The Network Security Analyst I performs advanced cybersecurity analysis and threat triage activities within the Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC). Work involves continuously monitoring, triaging, analyzing, and prioritizing cybersecurity alerts; investigating suspicious activity; identifying potential threats; and coordinating incident response activities to protect agency information systems, networks, and data. Serves as a primary point of contact for security event analysis, threat identification, and incident escalation.

Essential Job Functions

Monitors, analyzes, and triages cybersecurity alerts generated by Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), cloud security, email security, identity protection, and network security platforms.
Conducts initial investigations of detected and reported security events to determine severity, scope, impact, and potential risk to agency operations.
Identifies, validates, and prioritizes potential cybersecurity incidents, escalating confirmed threats to Incident Response, Threat Hunting, or SOC Engineering teams according to established procedures.
Correlates security events from multiple data sources, including endpoints (EDR), firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), intrusion prevention systems (IPS), cloud services, authentication systems, and threat intelligence feeds.
Reviews and analyzes indicators of compromise (IOCs), suspicious network activity, phishing emails, malware detections, and anomalous user behavior.
Documents investigations, findings, and response actions in ticketing and case management systems to ensure accurate tracking and reporting.
Assists with incident containment, eradication, and recovery efforts by coordinating with technical teams and stakeholders.
Reports and escalates to the CSOC Team Lead and/or SOC Manager.
Supports the continuous improvement of threat detection capabilities through alert tuning, process refinement, threat intelligence integration, and identification of false-positive trends.
Performs vulnerability assessment reviews and evaluates identified vulnerabilities for potential risk and remediation prioritization.
Supports development and maintenance of operational procedures, playbooks, workflows, and knowledge base articles related to threat detection and incident response.
Researches emerging cyber threats, attack techniques, tactics, and procedures (TTPs) to improve detection and response effectiveness.

FSA Federal (FSA) provides professional services supporting law enforcement and homeland security missions across the United States.

FSA Federal is seeking a detail-oriented Data Analyst to provide data, documentation, and administrative support to the U.S. Attorney's Office.

new_jobs.title: Credit Research Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Credit views on this bank's covered issuers currently rely on periodic reviews that go stale between rating cycles, and a global bank standing up its India technology and operations centre has partnered with Flexiple to hire a Credit Research Analyst who will keep those views current on its India credit research desk.
The desk you'd support

This desk covers a portfolio of corporate and financial issuers, tracking their credit profile, capital structure and covenant headroom, and feeding that analysis into the rating views and internal credit opinions used across lending, trading and risk functions. The work sits close to real decisions: a stale credit view here can show up as a mispriced position or a missed covenant breach somewhere else in the bank.
How a rating call gets made

Building and maintaining financial models for covered issuers, including leverage, coverage and liquidity metrics
Tracking covenant compliance, rating actions and credit events across the assigned portfolio
Drafting credit notes and issuer updates that summarise financial performance against thesis and triggers
Supporting senior analysts on new issuer onboarding, including first-pass credit write-ups
Monitoring macro, sector and regulatory developments that could move an issuer's credit profile

What we're looking for in a first read

2 to 6 years of experience in credit research, corporate ratings, fixed income research or related credit analysis, with strong financial modelling skills and comfort reading financial statements, indentures and credit agreements. You should be able to write a credit note that a senior analyst can sign off on with minimal rework, and be precise about assumptions in a leverage or coverage model.
Where the seat sits

The role is based out of Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Hyderabad or Pune, or Remote (India), working alongside a global credit research function with regular touchpoints across time zones.
After you apply

The process includes an HR Screening, a modelling or case assignment, a Technical Round with the credit team and a final Culture Fit conversation. One application here covers this opening and any other Flexiple-matched role that fits your experience, so there is no need to reapply.

The Role:

The Business Analyst – Zero Waste, Chemical, & Resource Management (SP2) provides analytical and operational support to GM’s global Zero Waste, Resource Management (RM), Chemical Management (CM), and biological control programs. This role enables data-driven decision making, effective budget management, and disciplined execution to enable the SP2 team to advance GM’s environmental, safety, and cost-optimization objectives.

The analyst partners closely with SP2 program leads, plant teams, Infrastructure & Corporate Citizenship (ICC), Procurement, Finance, EH&S, and external suppliers to ensure goals are set, tracked, and achieved across North America and globally

What You'll Do (Responsibilities):

Zero Waste program support

Support development, alignment, and annual refresh of global Zero Waste goals, targets, and roadmaps for SP2 programs.
Maintain dashboards and scorecards for Zero Waste performance (e.g., waste generation, diversion, recovery, and cost metrics) at plant, regional, and enterprise levels.
Track progress against site-level action plans, escalate gaps, and highlight best practices and high-performing sites.
Coordinate recurring Zero Waste governance routines (cadence, agendas, pre-read materials, action item tracking, and follow-up).

Resource Management (RM) and Chemical Management (CM) financial support

Support development of annual RM and CM budgets for US and Canada, including volume, rate, and savings assumptions.
Build and maintain budget tracking tools that connect forecasts, actuals, and variances at the program, supplier, and site levels.
Coordinate purchase order (PO) requests, shopping carts, and change requests for RM, CM, and related environmental services, ensuring alignment with budget and contracts.
Monitor PO status, goods receipts, and invoice issues; work with Finance, Procurement, and suppliers to resolve discrepancies.
Provide periodic and ad hoc spend analysis, including cost drivers, savings realization, and scenario analysis.

Zero Waste and Environmental Capex support

Support Zero Waste and related environmental capex planning by compiling site requests, business cases, and benefit estimates.
Track approval status, spend, and realized benefits of capex projects (e.g., equipment for waste reduction, segregation, logistics, and treatment).
Maintain a portfolio view of Zero Waste and environmental investments, including timing, risks, and interdependencies.

Biological control of Metal Removal Fluids (MRF) and Metal Removal Fluids Strategy Team (MRFST) support

Support SP2’s biological control responsibilities for MRF and MRFST, including program documentation, data collection, and routine reporting.
Coordinate with plants, vendors, and technical experts to monitor performance (e.g., treatment effectiveness, volumes, quality parameters, and operational issues).
Help identify optimization opportunities in dosing, equipment, logistics, and supplier performance to improve safety, reliability, and total cost.

Data, analytics, and insights

Analyze RM and CM safety incidents, near misses, and risk identifications to detect patterns, “read across” opportunities, and common tasks with elevated risk.
Develop visualizations and summaries that translate complex data into clear insights and recommendations for SP2 leadership and stakeholders.
Maintain and continuously improve standard reports, dashboards, and tools (e.g., in Excel, Power BI, or other GM-approved platforms).
Aggregate and analyze waste, recycling, and diversion data (volumes, materials, destinations, costs, and rebates) across sites to identify trends, outliers, and improvement opportunities.

Industry trends, technology, and benchmarking

Monitor external trends in waste reduction, waste handling and logistics, biological treatment, and chemical selection for indirect materials.
Summarize industry developments, regulatory changes, and emerging technologies with potential impact on GM’s Zero Waste, RM, and CM strategies.
Support pilots and evaluations of new technologies or service models, including data collection, KPI design, and results reporting.
Provide structured benchmarking against peer companies and best-in-class service models where data is available.

Governance, processes, and documentation

Maintain organized, current documentation for SP2 programs (standards, procedures, playbooks, training content, meeting notes, and decision logs).
Support development and refinement of common processes, templates, and tools for Zero Waste, RM, CM, and biological control.
Help ensure alignment with GM safety, compliance, and information management requirements in all SP2 program artifacts.
Coordinate cross-functional working sessions, workshops, and knowledge-sharing forums to disseminate lessons learned and best practices.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)
:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business, Data Analytics, or related fields
5+ years of experience in business analysis, data analytics, operations, EH&S, environmental programs, or related discipline.
Demonstrated experience with data analysis and reporting (Microsoft Excel; experience with tools such as Power BI or similar is a plus).
Experience supporting budgets, forecasts, or financial tracking (e.g., spend, variance analysis, savings tracking); familiarity with enterprise systems for POs and invoices (e.g., SAP or equivalent).
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills with the ability to work with large datasets and multiple systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to summarize complex topics and influence stakeholders at different levels.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and follow through on commitments with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

What Can Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

Experience in waste management, resource management, chemical management, environmental engineering, or industrial operations.
Familiarity with Zero Waste concepts, waste hierarchy, and recycling/landfill diversion strategies.
Experience working with safety data (incidents, near misses, risk assessments) and translating insights into practical risk-reduction actions.
Knowledge of biological treatment or biological control applications in material recovery, wastewater, or related environmental systems.
Experience working with manufacturing plants, logistics providers, and/or environmental service suppliers.
Demonstrated ability to develop or improve business processes, templates, and governance routines.

Procurement Performance and Support

Monitor commitments, purchase orders, vendor performance, invoice exceptions, open obligations, periods of performance, funding utilization, change exposure, and closeout status; escalate material exceptions with recommended actions.
Deliver spend, demand, and market analysis to support sourcing strategy, vendor management, budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow visibility, and procurement planning for EPC work.
Develop quantitative vendor and procurement performance measures, track action closure, and communicate findings, risks, and recommendations to technical, operational, commercial, and executive audiences.

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Data Analytics, Economics, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
At least 3 years of directly relevant analytical experience; 5 to 7 years of progressively responsible experience preferred, ideally supporting project-based or capital-intensive operations.
Advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI capability, plus experience extracting and reconciling data from SAP or another enterprise resource planning platform.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, validate data, quantify business impact, communicate with executives, and drive cross-functional actions to closure.

Experience in EPC, construction, engineering, industrial, nuclear, energy, federal contracting, or another regulated, project-driven environment.
Working knowledge of procurement lifecycle management, strategic sourcing, vendor performance, purchase-order administration, procure-to-pay, spend analytics, invoice reconciliation, commitments, funding, and periods of performance.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Here at the Office for National Statistics (ONS), we have unrivalled access to a vast breadth and depth of data. Every day, we use this to produce trusted statistics and insightful analysis that informs both the public and policymakers on the issues that matter most.

Our work spans the production of essential economic statistics and the analysis that brings them to life to support decision makers and help people understand the UK economy. Our key focus is producing high quality, relevant and timely core statistics: gross domestic product, inflation, public sector finances, labour market statistics, trade and the balance of payments. We're also expanding our use of administrative data, while transforming our surveys and moving off legacy statistical systems.

Following the recent independent review of ONS by Sir Robert Devereux, we’ve launched our Economic Statistics Plan (ESP)—a bold response to restore quality and confidence in our economic statistics. The plan outlines how we assess the quality of our core outputs, the steps we’re taking to address risks and challenges, and the foundations we’re laying for the future. These changes will help us build a more resilient statistical system that supports confident decision-making and a clearer understanding of UK society.

Delivering the ESP successfully requires a collective effort. As part of that, ONS is recruiting a number of Data Analysts to help us understand, manipulate, and accurately analyse data—providing insight that informs both internal and external audiences. You will play a key role in delivering the Plan, and in developing our people, building good working relationships across the organisation and making ONS a great place to work.

We’re particularly interested to hear from applicants with experience with economic data sources, such as business surveys; or a background in economics, finance, or accountancy.

Job Description

Data analysts collect, organise and study data to provide business and operational insight. They work across a broad range of areas and topics.

Data analysts understand, manipulate and accurately analyse data to provide insight about a topic for internal and external audiences. They make complex topics easier for everyone to understand, including non-specialist audiences.

Key Responsibilities Of Data Analysts Include

manage, clean, abstract and aggregate data alongside a range of analytical studies on that data
identify, collect and migrate data to and from a range of systems
manipulate and link different data sets
help with data quality checking and cleaning
use tools and techniques for data analysis, data visualisation and provision of business insight
present data and conclusions logically and concisely in the most appropriate format, while following the Analysis Function standards
summarise and present the results of data analysis to a range of customers — this includes making recommendations for how to use the data
interpret and apply relevant data information security standards, policies and procedures to data
perform routine statistical analysis and answer queries, which may include the production of reports
use a range of analytical techniques such as data mining, time series, forecasting and modelling techniques to identify and predict trends in data
work with data architecture
use coding and programming skills for data and analytics

Please note we will not be badging to an analytical profession as part of this campaign. However, there are regular opportunities for staff to apply for badging with the relevant government analytical profession upon joining ONS.

Person specification

Essential Criteria -

Data Analysis (Lead Criterion): Ability to interpret and work with diverse data sets, identifying trends, resolving issues, and using programming tools to analyse and assure data quality.
Effective Communication: Ability to identify and clearly communicate trends, insights, and anomalies in data to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leaders.
Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration: Demonstrable ability to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders, building strong working relationships to support shared objectives.

Qualifications

We welcome applications from individuals who satisfy the essential criteria and are a member of, or eligible to join, one of eligibility for the government analytical professions as listed below :

Government Economic Service (GES),
Government Statistical Service (GSS),
Government Operational Research Service (GORS), or
Government Social Research (GSR).

To achieve this, candidates need to hold at least;

A 2.2 degree in economics, OR
A 2.2 in a social science related subject with sufficient research OR
A 2:2 in a numerate subject containing taught statistical content

OR

A minimum 2 years relevant work experience

Please note - All candidates are expected to ensure they meet the entry requirements. Failure to demonstrate how you meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Making Effective Decisions
Communicating and Influencing
Working Together

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

Data Quality - Understands and can explain statistical / research methods and the differences between sources, such as concepts or different data sets. Is able to design and choose best methods for data collection.
Analysis Approach - Utilises analytical tools to analyse data for trends and gaps, applying approved techniques to create coherent series’ and data modelling
Presentation / Dissemination - Communicates in a straightforward and engaging manner, choosing appropriate styles to maximise understanding.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £34,587, Office for National Statistics contributes £10,019 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our 5400 valued colleagues across the business.

Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that the benefits pack attached (bottom of page)
will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture.

Inclusion & Accessibility

At ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.

If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Experience and Technical skills.

Security Clearance

For ONS the requirement for SC clearance is to have been present in the UK for 3 consecutive years immediately prior to applying
and the department will consider eligibility by exception on a case-by-case basis. You will be asked to provide information regarding your UK residency during your application, and failure to provide this will result in your application being rejected.

At the point of SC application, you will need to provide or give access to the following evidence:

Visa Sponsorship

ONS are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants are expected to hold a valid right to work in the UK when employment commences. If you are applying on a time-limited visa, this will need to be valid for at least 18 months at point of application.

To work at ONS, applicants must meet the Civil Service nationality requirements, satisfy UK right to work requirements and, where applicable, meet the relevant security clearance requirements. If you are unsure whether you meet the appropriate right to work or security clearance eligibility criteria, please refer to the guidance on Gov.uk or contact the recruitment email provided in the advert before applying
. Failure to meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected and employment offers being withdrawn.

Application Process

of the lead criteria -

Examples that do not meet the minimum standard will not proceed to full sift stage.

Please note that Success Profiles Behaviour examples are not required at this stage of the application process.

When a high volume of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted. Analyze operational, supply chain, financial, and business data to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities.

Quantify the financial impact of proposed initiatives and operational changes.

Collect, cleanse, validate, and analyze data from multiple enterprise systems.

Master's degree in Operations Research, or related discipline.

Experience applying quantitative methods to solve business problems.
Experience working with large datasets and analytical tools.

Knowledge of optimization techniques, linear programming, simulation, forecasting, and statistical analysis.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Experience with Python, R, SQL, or other analytical programming languages.
Familiarity with Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization tools.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Ability to explain complex concepts to non-technical audiences.
Strong project management and organizational skills.

Preferred Skills

Experience with supply chain optimization and inventory management.
Knowledge of machine learning and predictive analytics.
Familiarity with SAP ERP.
Experience with optimization mathematics and tools such as Gurobi, CPLEX, SAS, or AnyLogic.

Work Environment

Full-time office environment with collaboration across multiple business functions.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
Occasional travel may be required to support operational sites and project initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile

A successful Operations Research Analyst combines strong quantitative and technical capabilities with business acumen. They are curious, detail-oriented, and able to transform complex data into practical recommendations that improve operational and financial outcomes.

new_jobs.title: Investment Product Strategy Analyst
new_jobs.description:
PortfolioFuture is an investment research platform focused on exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and mutual funds. We use empirical research to identify comparable funds, evaluate stronger alternatives, and help investors better understand how investment products differ in practice.

Role Description

The Investment Product Strategy Analyst is a remote role focused on how investment research is positioned, communicated, and distributed to the market.

The role combines investment-product research, product positioning, audience analysis, content development, and distribution. You will work with PortfolioFuture’s ETF and mutual fund research, understand how investment products compete for attention, develop clear market-facing communication, and help expand the reach of PortfolioFuture’s research among investors, financial advisors, asset managers, and other industry professionals.

Responsibilities

Research ETFs, mutual funds, competing products, and relevant market developments.
Translate PortfolioFuture’s research into clear product insights and market-facing communication.
Analyze how investment products are positioned, differentiated, and discussed in the market.
Develop content and messaging around fund research, product comparisons, and investment themes.
Support distribution across LinkedIn, email, web, and other professional channels.
Research investors, financial advisors, asset managers, media, and other relevant audiences.
Identify new channels, communities, and distribution opportunities for PortfolioFuture’s research.
Test positioning, messaging, formats, and campaign ideas.
Track engagement, traffic, audience growth, and distribution performance.
Use AI and digital tools to improve research, communication, and distribution workflows.
Support broader product, research, and growth initiatives as PortfolioFuture develops.

Professional Exposure

The role provides direct exposure to investment products, product strategy, research communication, positioning, digital distribution, and audience development. You will work with real ETF and mutual fund research and gain visibility into how investment products are presented, evaluated, and distributed across asset management and wealth management.

For eligible F-1 students, this role can be structured to support CPT requirements, subject to university approval.

Qualifications

Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Interest in financial markets, ETFs, mutual funds, fintech, or investment products.
Ability to understand analytical information and communicate it clearly.
Strong research instincts and attention to detail.
Interest in how investment products are positioned and distributed.
Familiarity with LinkedIn, digital publishing, email, web content, or other distribution channels is helpful.
Ability to organize and execute projects independently.
Experience in finance, economics, business, marketing, communications, journalism, media, or related activities is helpful but not required.
Comfort using AI and digital tools to improve productivity.

Startup Environment

PortfolioFuture is an early-stage company. The role is hands-on, priorities can evolve quickly, and there are limited layers of management. Team members are expected to work independently, take ownership, and contribute beyond a narrow job description when needed.

Visit https://portfoliofuture.com/ to learn more.
